text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgarians withdrew some four billion levs from the State Savings Bank on Monday as people rushed to convert levs to foreign currency because of uncertainty over the possible impact of a currency board on the banking system, bank officials said.
-- Police on Thursday arrested Anton Belchev, son of former finance minister Belcho Belchev, on charges of money laundering and illegally mailing some $7 million abroad, an unnamed prosecutor said.
-- The European Commission is expected to approve imports of Bulgarian cheese with a customs tariff discount of 80 percent under the agreement for the association of Bulgaria in the EU.

-- Bulgaria's opposition is ready to take responsibility for the ruling of the country only if early parliamentary elections are held, opposition leaders said at a meeting with President Zhelyu Zhelev.

-- Bulgarian customs officers said they had seized some nine million levs worth of pirated compact discs hidden in a bus owned by Bulgarian private company Etap Adress at the Yugoslav border crossing of Kalotina.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to raise electricity prices again by 15 percent effective from December 1, government officials said. Last week, electricity was increased by 9.7 percent.

-- "Bulgarians should not worry about their lev deposits in Bulgaria's State Savings Bank as whatever happens the SSB will remain a reliable institution," said Bulgarian National Bank governor Lyubomir Filipov.
-- The Sofia municipality will sell at a tender 49 percent of the municipal water supply company, a senior municipal official said. -- Sofia Newsroom +3592 981 8569
